record.original_question: Can strong normalization of typed lambda calculus be proved by a reasonably straightforward mapping from typed terms to a well-founded ordering, even though beta-reduction can leave the type structure unchanged? Does the same approach work for polymorphic, second-order lambda calculus?

evidence.quote: Can strong normalization of the typed lambda calculus be proved by a reasonably straightforward mapping from typed terms to a well-founded ordering?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the simply typed lambda calculus, whose terms are built from variables, applications, and lambda abstractions, and whose types are built from base types using the function-type constructor →. β-reduction is the rewriting relation generated by (λx:A. M) N → M[x := N]. The system is strongly normalizing: every β-reduction sequence terminates.

(a) Does there exist a "reasonably straightforward" map Φ from well-typed simply typed lambda terms into a well-founded ordering (W, <) with the property that whenever M →_β M' one has Φ(M') < Φ(M), so that strong normalization follows directly from well-foundedness of (W, <)? The challenge is that a β-redex (λx:A. M) N and its contractum M[x := N] may have identical type structure, so Φ cannot simply read off type information in a naive way.

(b) Does the same kind of straightforward mapping into a well-founded ordering yield a strong normalization proof for the polymorphic (second-order) lambda calculus, i.e. System F, where types include universally quantified type variables and reduction includes type-abstraction/type-application β-reduction?
artifact.status_search_result: For the simply typed lambda calculus, recent work (Van Oostrom and Wiedijk, "Two Decreasing Measures for Simply Typed λ-Terms", FSCD 2023) gives explicit decreasing measures from typed terms into well-founded orderings (natural numbers and nested multisets), affirmatively answering part (a). Earlier works (e.g. Gandy, de Vrijer, Joachimski–Matthes, Loader) had also developed such measure-based proofs. For System F / second-order polymorphic lambda calculus, no simple measure-based mapping into a well-founded ordering is known; standard proofs rely on Girard's reducibility candidates, and a "reasonably straightforward" ordinal-style mapping remains elusive. Hence part (b) appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Two Decreasing Measures for Simply Typed λ-Terms
status_evidence.snippet: A decreasing measure is a function that maps each typable λ-term to an element of a well-founded ordering, in such a way that contracting any β-redex decreases the value of the function, entailing strong normalization.
status_evidence.claim: For simply typed lambda calculus, explicit decreasing measures into well-founded orderings have been constructed, addressing part (a).

status_evidence.title: Strong Normalization in a Non-Deterministic Typed Lambda-Calculus
status_evidence.snippet: A method to prove strong-normalization for typed-calculi uses a decreasing metric over a well-founded ordering.
status_evidence.claim: Measure-based methods for strong normalization in typed lambda calculi are an established line of work.
